generatedBy: DSP detection (measured) + vision naming pass following PROMPT.md
note: Timings, loudness, duration and behaviour are measured from the waveform. Text, visibility and frame position come from the naming pass. Speech is left to Whisper and is not included here.

cues.note: Measured: sustained bed 4.78-11.75s, centroid 857 Hz, mean loudness 0.31 of peak. Low and rising. Nothing on screen accounts for it — the picture is a blizzard, which is its own visible thing. The drone is the film telling you something is coming.

The loudest and sharpest event in the film — loudness 1.00, onset strength 1.00, centroid 1333 Hz. It lands on a black title card. There is nothing on screen at all. This is the single clearest case in the whole trailer for a caption: the sound IS the moment, and a hearing viewer gets the entire jolt of it.

Measured: loudness 0.92, centroid 1047 Hz, 1.6s. Frame shows Sintel swinging a spear overhead in the blizzard. The swing is visible; the weight and hardness of the impact is not. Marked partly visible, so it renders at reduced intensity rather than being dropped.

Measured: 7 seconds, rising RMS, centroid 2106 Hz — bright, strings and brass. Under a run through ruins at sunset. Standard captions give this two seconds of [dramatic music] and then leave a Deaf viewer in silence for the rest of the build.

Measured: loudness 0.99, onset strength 0.77, centroid 2359 Hz — the brightest sustained passage in the film. The emotional peak, over the shot of Sintel with the dragon. Held for its real length instead of flashed once.

Measured: loudness 0.75, centroid 756 Hz — much darker than the peak, and falling. Over the empty desert. The release after a climax is as structural as the build, and captions today have no way to say it.
Measured: 6 seconds, loudness 0.94, centroid 1523 Hz. Over the SINTEL title. Nothing visual carries it.
Measured: loudness 0.94, centroid 959 Hz, falling. On the logo, black screen. The film ends on a sound, and only a sound.

suppressed.reason: The screen is filled with driving snow across dark peaks. A Deaf viewer can see that it is windy. Captioning it would occupy the frame to say something the picture already says louder.

suppressed.candidate: a gust, or a footfall in snow
suppressed.reason: Measured loudness 0.56, centroid 976 Hz. Sintel is on screen walking through whiteout. Both plausible sources are visible.
Measured loudness 0.66, centroid 586 Hz. Arrives 0.9s after the spear strike already captioned. Two captions for one action reads as stutter.
Same musical passage already captured by s4 and s5. The detector fired six times inside one crescendo. Merged rather than repeated.
Measured loudness only 0.36, centroid 2592 Hz, 0.43s. Real, but quiet and ambiguous. Below the density threshold — not every sound earns a caption.

notCaptioned.speech: The shaman speaks from roughly 12.2s and Sintel from roughly 14s and 23s. Speech is Whisper's job, transcribed verbatim in the browser, and is deliberately not invented here.
